entries.text: VERB ask. Use kmp_ask for a semantic question that stored evidence can answer. To enumerate a period — yesterday, since, what changed, current or latest — navigate time instead. When the semantic question carries a date or a range, it is still one Ask: pass the half-open UTC interval as interval, or the instant as as_of, and axis when the question is about when something was seen, written or held rather than when it happened; the kernel admits only what falls inside, reads supersession and expiry as they stood then, and declares where it stood in proof.interval, proof.as_of and proof.axis. Minimum input: exact about and the question rendered in plain English with every number, identifier and acronym the user wrote kept exactly, plus the user's own words as asked_as. Expect: cited stored text byte for byte or UNKNOWN, asked_as echoed, a warning when the rendering dropped an identifier or leans to another language, and on UNKNOWN within an interval the nearest match outside it in proof.nearest_outside, which is the cue to widen the interval rather than conclude the memory was never written. Next: inspect a relied-on ref, trace a relied-on connection, re-ask at most once in the user's own words, or stop honestly at UNKNOWN. After the permitted selections, a genuinely semantic UNKNOWN is terminal. Do not inspect the root, sweep all abouts, change optional arguments or traverse the graph to bypass it. Reclassify only when the original goal actually asks for temporal state. Read the language and retrieved-proof topics when their warnings or provenance matter. For a partial read, execute projection.next_action with its complete arguments, preserving question, asked_as, dimensions and temporal selection. If core_text_shortened, its call restarts without page.cursor at a sufficient allowance; discard the earlier partial reconstruction. Otherwise append only expansion beyond each section core. Finish when next_action is null; detail or selection caps remain explicit. A stale cursor returns conflict and feedback[].action for a fresh read; never combine different selections.
entries.evidence: The live kmp_ask contract retrieves stored evidence and never generates a fallback answer.

entries.text: VERB relate. Use kmp_relate when the question is what the memories of several abouts have to do with each other: which facts of these projects fell in the release window, how they stand to each other in time inside the labels they share (the same dimension kind and scope; a scope under two kinds is two labels), what each about declared between its own facts, and which declared contradictions still stand. Coordinate comparisons are read off the stored coordinates and do not declare links. Cross-about identity links are separate writer declarations from a relate proposal. Minimum input: the current about and dimensions.scope naming or sweeping the abouts; interval and axis bound it in time. Expect: facts with their lifecycle state at the end of the interval, declared relations within each about, coordinate relations between abouts with a why a reader can check against the coordinates, tensions, proposed links between facts of different abouts that share a key — an identifier rare across the span, a matching English summary, a proper name — with the signals that read them and never stored, and a proof that says which abouts were read and which had nothing inside. A proposal a writer declares with kmp_write_memory as same_event_as or same_entity_as comes back declared, and from then on ask cites through it across abouts and trace walks it. Next: inspect a fact before relying on it; ask when what you want is an answer to a question rather than the shape of what happened. budget.max_bytes pages whole items in facts, declared, coordinate, tensions and proposed order. Preserve the selection when following page.next_cursor. If no item fits, page.required_bytes gives the allowance for the next whole item; a large summary or selection proof is a stable floor returned with an explicit warning. Follow next_actions as complete tool/arguments calls. The opaque cursor binds the request and the complete selected content, including facts or proof on later pages. A change returns conflict with feedback action to restart; never combine earlier pages with that fresh read.
entries.evidence: The live kmp_relate contract returns facts, declared, coordinate and tensions with a proof and never ranks by a question.

Native field projection checks omitted fields, executable scoped expansion, unchanged proof and cursor rejection after hidden content changes across embedded and gRPC transports. The shared relation-clock fix from #599 also checks link timestamps independently of older endpoints before constructing proof and lifecycle. Direct native interval regressions cover both directions, start ties, exclusive ends, proof paging, earlier antecedents, later proof exclusion and unassessed expiry without an end. The four live temporal contracts define direction, cursor field, ordering and continuation semantics separately. A real embedded MCP regression combines lane selection with positive and negative selectors through all four temporal verbs and clocks, and the negotiated App projection. Native wake/ask rejects explicitly later receipt evidence from earlier observed instants and exclusive interval ends while preserving event-time retrieval. Native response-page tests reconstruct entries and proof verbatim, reject a changed selection and execute the minimum-budget retry; completed packets offer executable temporal navigation. The limited-selection warning leaves continuation syntax to the transport; MCP actions do not reinterpret an opaque response cursor as a memory ref. Goto proof stops at its inclusive resolved cursor or an earlier exclusive interval end, respecting later relation and evidence arrival.

entries.text: VERB audit. Use kmp_inspect when one ref must support a claim; use kmp_trace when the connection between two refs is itself the claim. Do not guess or rebuild refs. Minimum input: exact about and exact returned refs. Expect: canonical object, evidence and links, or an ordered proof path. Next: follow pagination and cite stored evidence byte-for-byte. Inspect uses the owning about. Trace can cross a declared, evidenced same_event_as or same_entity_as edge; naming a foreign endpoint alone creates no path. Inspect keeps the stored object stable and pages expandable evidence and links; budget guidance distinguishes the stable floor from omitted expansion. Use include.raw for audit records, not for routine lesson reading. After retaining the first inspect object, continue with page.cursor and page.repeat_object=false to receive only object.ref plus the remaining expansion. object_reused=true declares that reuse. Keep the original text, kind, metadata and source; do not replace them with the ref-only object. Execute Inspect next_actions to continue with the complete bound call. If no whole item fits, page.minimum_progress_bytes names a sufficient next-item allowance. The action offers at least that much and prefers the complete inspection up to the usual 10,000-byte budget, avoiding a one-item-per-call walk. page.required_bytes still sizes the complete inspection. A fixed budget means the result remains partial. A changed object or selected proof returns conflict and a complete restart in feedback; that fresh read returns the new full object even if prior pages reused it. Omit repeat_object to receive the full object on every page. Trace also pages whole relations under budget.max_bytes. If page.returned is zero and page.has_more is true, this is pending proof, not an absent path: retry the same page.next_cursor with budget.max_bytes at least page.required_bytes. Trace next_actions contain the exact continuation. A changed endpoint or selected proof, including a later edge, rejects the cursor with a complete fresh-read action in feedback. The cursor is not a persisted snapshot; restart instead of mixing old pages with new evidence. For a write receipt, execute the returned receipt.action: object.text is immutable accepted-command JSON containing canonical_memory, writer diagnostics and command revision/hash. It is not the current state of the memories. Receipt refs stay within their owning about and do not enter graph traversal.
entries.evidence: The live Inspect contract returns executable continuation, minimum-progress and stale-selection restart calls, preserving the about boundary, object reuse and canonical proof. Receipt inspection uses the existing accepted-command index without creating a graph memory.

The installed guide/AGENT.md is a brief entry with exact references to extended verbs and examples. Read it once while it remains in context; a routine memory call needs no full documentation wake. Sync converges both fixed guide abouts idempotently through kmp-guide-sync.sh; it writes the selected store and may update its maintained bundle. entries.text: VERB setup, lexical bridge. The table that lets ask reach a memory written in another language is installed by kmp-mcp setup and kmp-mcp update, once for the machine at <user data home>/kmp/lexical-bridge.kmpb, never inside one store. Three places are read, nearest first: whatever KMP_LEXICAL_BRIDGE names, then <data dir>/lexical-bridge.kmpb for one store alone, then the machine's table. Decline it with --no-lexical-bridge, or install one built locally with --lexical-bridge FILE. The release's table replaces whatever the machine held, and the receipt names the digest it replaced under replaced_sha256; a table that must outlive update lives beside one store or is named by KMP_LEXICAL_BRIDGE. It is never a gate: a release that publishes no table and a fetch that fails both leave setup successful, and the receipt says which happened under lexical_bridge. Expect: crosses_languages true once a table is in place. Without the table, original text and valid summary_en remain searchable; an English summary can retrieve an original in another language. The table is an additional path, not a requirement for every cross-language retrieval. info and doctor report its availability.
entries.evidence: The convergence installs the table last, after the engine is proved, and maps every failure onto a reported outcome rather than an error.

entries.text: One idempotency key names one logical write or view intent. An exact retry with the same key is success without a duplicate. Reusing a key for different content is a conflict and must not be worked around by blind retry.

entries.text: A partial read is not the whole answer. Follow page.next_cursor with every bound argument unchanged; wake and Ask page expansion items, temporal verbs page entries and proof through executable next_actions, trace pages relations, and inspect pages details, evidence and links. required_bytes is negotiation guidance, not a reason to probe budgets repeatedly. Ask keeps cited evidence in the stable core and preserves retrieval rank among additional evidence across pages. A changed candidate order invalidates an old cursor. If a wake or Ask page returns zero expansion items while has_more is true, follow its no-progress guidance: increase budget.max_bytes for the same cursor, or report the selection as partial when the budget is fixed. Repeating that cursor at the same byte ceiling cannot advance. Trace and Relate provide complete next_actions. Only page.entries and budget.max_bytes can vary on their continuation; changing selected content or another argument returns conflict with a restart action in feedback.
entries.evidence: Every bounded live read reports its own page unit, continuation and byte-budget guidance.

entries.text: budget.max_bytes is the normative host-safe ceiling for serialized structuredContent. On kmp_ask, kmp_wake, temporal reads, kmp_inspect, kmp_trace and kmp_relate, a ceiling below the response's stable floor returns that minimal floor with a warning naming the requested and required sizes; it is a qualified success, not an error or permission to discard the stable object. Values below 512 bytes remain invalid. Raise the ceiling only when richer expansion is needed. A shortened proof body retains its identity and provenance. Ask and Wake return an executable projection.next_action. When core_text_shortened is true, it restarts without page.cursor at a sufficient allowance to recover the full core; discard the partial reconstruction. Otherwise append only expansion beyond each section core. Continue until next_action is null: has_more=false alone describes expansion, not restored core. A stalled page declares minimum_progress_bytes and proposes that allowance plus 10000 bytes for useful expansion, so restoring the core does not force a one-item walk. If that allowance is unavailable, keep the result partial. Cursor conflicts include feedback[].action to restart the same arguments; do not combine old and new selections. budget.detail chooses eligible expansion before caps: excluded_by_detail is not lost pagination. budget.max_entries caps the selection before paging. budget.tokens is an advisory planning hint, not a filter of canonical structuredContent; defaults remain declared in each tool schema. selection_omitted includes evidence withheld by max_entries before response projection, even when page.has_more is false or compact detail hides the missing-source list. A completed page can still describe a capped selection; changing the cap starts a new selection. Inspect can avoid repeating a large stable object: retain it from the first page, then use page.repeat_object=false with the returned cursor. This can let the remaining evidence fit the original ceiling. required_bytes still describes the complete inspection with its full object. Execute Inspect next_actions until empty; when an expansion item cannot fit, the call offers at least page.minimum_progress_bytes, preferring a complete inspection up to the usual 10,000-byte allowance. If that allowance is unavailable, report the pending proof. A changed selection returns conflict with a fresh-read action, which restores the full object. Trace and Relate never shorten a fact, relation why or evidence to fit a page. For example, after a 512-byte request returns zero items, copy page.next_cursor and set budget.max_bytes to page.required_bytes; do not repeat the blocked page at 512 bytes. Their opaque cursors bind the complete selected content. Execute next_actions to retain every argument and any negotiated byte allowance. Changed content returns a conflict with a complete restart action; retain the old result only as an explicitly incomplete earlier read. Temporal pages report minimum_progress_bytes when the next indivisible item cannot fit, and next_actions provides a retry that admits an item. A response page can be complete while selection.has_more reports history outside the selected packet.
entries.evidence: The live read schemas and projections guarantee one stable response floor plus an explicit warning when a valid max_bytes ceiling cannot contain a smaller honest response.

KMP proof separates superseded, conflicts and expired so an agent cannot flatten distinct lifecycles. Native historical wake/ask preserves an earlier conflict and hides its live marker only after explicit supersession; the old edge remains auditable.

entries.text: Ask proof can carry memory the question never matched. An evidence item with reached_by arrived by a route instead of by its words: relation means a proven causal or motivational edge was walked out from something the question did match, named by reached_from, reached_via and reached_hops; association means this store's own vocabulary connects the question's words to that memory's; bridge means the installed lexical-bridge table connects a few of the question's words to that memory's across a language, and reached_via lists the pairs, as valvula≈valve 0.51. Read them as proof and never as the answer. They are not cited in because, and the kernel makes no claim that they answer anything. A cited item may instead carry bridged_terms: it answered, most of the question reached it through the table rather than in the reader's own words, and confidence is medium at most for that reason. A cited item carrying restated_from and restated_via is the same thing as a cited memory in other words: a writer declared it with restates, same_event_as or same_entity_as, with why and evidence, and the kernel cites it beside the memory the question matched. With the optional local semantic retriever enabled on an embedded store, reached_by=semantic identifies a candidate proposed by the optional local retrieval adapter; semantic_model_revision records its version, including the ranking policy when the optional sidecar fuses BM25 and dense candidates. The default sidecar remains dense; a policy-qualified revision is required to opt in to lexical/dense fusion. The separate-bm25-v1 policy returns independent dense and BM25 channels for one native fusion; retrieval_channel identifies the supplemental representation retained, while similarity or a lexical score still does not prove an answer. KMP accepts only a matching stored ref and text fingerprint inside the selected scope, time and lifecycle. These candidates also remain proof rather than citations or answers; UNKNOWN may still be correct. A warning declares a fallback when the optional encoder is unavailable.
entries.evidence: The live ask projection marks indirectly reached evidence and keeps it out of the answer core; a cited item that crossed a language names the word pairs that carried it, and a cited restatement names the memory it restates.
kmp_ask takes asked_as, echoes it, and returns a warning per rendering fault; kmp-mcp info and doctor name the table a store reads or say there is none; the config verb takes no language setting.

entries.text: An English search summary is searched and never cited. A memory written in any language may carry the reserved entry metadata key summary_en: an English rendering of its text, written by the writer at ingest, that an English question lands on. kmp_ask searches it as content, beside the text, and cites the stored text byte for byte, so the summary is where a writer canonicalises jargon, rollout slipped as launch postponed, while the memory stays what somebody wrote. A cited item carrying matched_via: summary was reached through the rendering and not through its text, and summary_terms names the question's words the rendering supplied; read them as the writer's words, not the memory's. The kernel lints it rather than trusting it: kmp_ingest warns, entry by entry, about a summary that leans to another language, carries fewer than two informative words, repeats the text word for word, or drops an identifier the text carries such as v0.7.0, #469 or kmp-mcp, and ranking makes the same reading, so such a summary carries nothing. kmp_write_memory takes it as memories[].summary_en: a strict write requires it when the fact is not written in English and refuses one that fails the lint, naming every fault. Fix the summary the error names; never alter the text to fit it. A memory written before summaries existed still owes one: kmp-mcp summaries pending lists them and the doctor counts them; attach one or more with kmp_write_memory, search_summaries containing ref and summary_en only, and the stored text stays exactly as it was. The lint preserves literal identifiers: render UE as UE (EU), and retain source tokens such as 2026, 09:00 and UTC even if also adding an ISO date. It does not infer equivalent acronyms or dates. The writer returns independent record failures together; repair every feedback item and resend the whole packet. Further failures in a record may appear after its first error is fixed.
entries.evidence: The ingest translation lints summary_en against the entry text and reports each fault as a warning; the answer ranker scores a summary that passes the same lint as content, notes the words it supplied on the citation, and cites the entry text. The summaries verb and the doctor read the same list off the store's event log; search_summaries compiles to an ingest of the stored entry with the summary added to its metadata.

relations.why: The invocation gate constrains when any verb may be called at all, wake included: memory is entered when it is asked for, not because it is installed.
relations.evidence: The MCP initialize instructions open with a memory-routing gate whose default is on_request.

relations.why: Wake is the entry verb because known work must be recovered before any narrower route is chosen.

relations.why: Semantic Ask is chosen only after wake establishes the exact about and leaves a genuinely semantic gap.
relations.evidence: Wake returns current state; Ask retrieves evidence for the remaining non-temporal question.

relations.why: Ask answers a question from evidence; relate reads the shape of what several abouts hold in a span without a question to rank by. The one is chosen when the user wants an answer, the other when the user wants to see how memories of different projects stand to each other.
relations.evidence: The live kmp_relate contract ranks nothing and returns coordinate relations declared by nobody; kmp_ask cites evidence for a question.

relations.why: Temporal navigation corrects the route when the original request asks what a period holds rather than for an answer; a semantic question that carries a date stays an Ask and stands where it was asked with as_of or interval.
relations.evidence: The live router contract gives temporal intent precedence over Ask in two shapes: enumeration through the temporal verbs, and a dated Ask bounded by as_of or interval.

relations.why: Inspection or tracing audits the exact refs retained by semantic retrieval.
relations.evidence: Ask returns refs; inspect and trace preserve their stored proof.

relations.why: A related durable write should be grounded in refs the agent actually read rather than reconstructed context.

relations.why: Idempotency constrains retry behavior for every logical write.

relations.why: Temporal and bounded reads are truthful only when their continuation is consumed or disclosed.

relations.why: The stable response floor constrains byte-budget handling so a small valid ceiling cannot turn a bounded read into an error or silently erase its canonical object.

relations.why: An answer must preserve whether older evidence was replaced, remains conflicting or merely expired.

entries.text: KMP remembers why. This is the human guide: five short ideas first, then the deeper mechanics when you want them. Ask your agent to run open:guide whenever you want this view back.
entries.evidence: This is the person-facing guide shipped with the KMP plugin.

entries.text: KMP stores durable decisions and evidence, not transcripts. The useful unit is what changed, why it changed and what proves it.
entries.evidence: The public product contract defines memory as decisions and evidence rather than conversation logs.

entries.text: Embedded KMP runs on your machine. Codex and Claude Code can use the same local SQLite store; no KMP account or hosted memory service is required.
entries.evidence: The embedded engine selects SQLite in WAL mode and the viewer binds to loopback.

entries.text: Memory keeps the words its writer stored. The writer can also add an English search summary, summary_en, so an English question can reach memory written in another language without translating the original. KMP searches a valid summary but cites the original text. An optional table of word pairs adds another way to cross languages; setup installs it once for your machine and doctor reports whether it is available. Without the table, stored text and valid summaries remain searchable. None of these search paths runs a language model.
entries.evidence: A citation reached through the writer's summary carries matched_via: summary and summary_terms while preserving the original text. A citation reached through a lexical bridge names its word pairs in bridged_terms, at medium confidence at most.

entries.text: A repository can publish selected project memory in .kmp/memory.jsonl. A clone inherits that reviewed bundle; private abouts in a shared user store stay out unless explicitly exported, and release-owned KMP guides stay local because the installed plugin supplies them.
entries.evidence: Commit-native publication and Doctor apply the same authored-memory projection, excluding guide:kmp and guide:kmp-agent while explicit backup export retains the full store.

entries.text: Say: show me the memory behind this decision. Your agent retrieves the evidence and guides the same view you see. ChronoLoom names who moved it and why. Take control keeps the current frame; Undo reverses the last memory-view move. Compare abouts as 3D planes or flatten the same scene, filter by labels, and move or resize the shared time window in either camera. A loading indicator stays visible while clocks, layers or evidence update; the content dims and fades back in when ready. Reduced motion keeps the status without animation.
entries.evidence: The three semantic view tools share one revisioned ChronoLoom state between agent and person.

entries.text: The difference between occurred and observed time is the event boundary versus the knowledge boundary. KMP keeps four clocks because they answer different questions. Occurred time is when the event happened. Observed time is when a source or agent learned it. Ingested time is when the kernel committed it. Validity is the interval in which a state applies.
entries.evidence: The memory coordinate contract stores occurred_at, observed_at, ingested_at, valid_from and exclusive valid_until separately.

entries.text: budget.max_bytes limits how much structured response a host receives. If a valid ceiling is smaller than KMP's minimal honest response, KMP returns that stable floor with a warning naming both sizes instead of failing or hiding the canonical object. Values below 512 bytes are invalid; raise the ceiling only when you need richer detail. A cited memory stays identifiable when its preview is shortened. Ask and Wake now return the complete call for continuing or restoring a shortened preview. A restoration starts a new read with enough bytes; its agent discards the partial reconstruction. It can also inspect the cited memory for its full text. Finishing expansion alone does not prove the preview is complete. An optional local semantic encoder can help the embedded engine find differently worded sources. Similarity is shown as retrieval evidence and never establishes an answer on its own; an unavailable encoder leaves ordinary retrieval available with a warning. Ask keeps cited memories first and returns additional evidence in retrieval order, including when it spans several pages. If a page cannot fit the next item, KMP says that it cannot advance: allow a larger response or keep the result explicitly partial. An agent that retained the first inspected object can request later pages with page.repeat_object=false. KMP sends its ref and the remaining proof, marks object_reused, and rejects the continuation if the object or selected evidence changed.
entries.evidence: The shipped read contracts preserve a stable response floor and make every byte-budget exception visible as a warning.

entries.text: Supersession is not contradiction. A superseding memory replaces an older state and keeps the old reasoning as history. A contradiction leaves two live claims in tension until something resolves them.
entries.evidence: KMP proof reports superseded entries and live conflicts in separate fields.

entries.text: Named snapshots are deliberate recovery points. Content-addressed exports are deterministic heads. Bundle merge only fast-forwards identical history or an exact prefix; KMP refuses to invent order for divergent branches.
entries.evidence: The format-3 bundle contract binds content digest, about coverage and event range before import or merge.

entries.text: Two hosts can share one embedded store. SQLite WAL allows independent Codex and Claude processes to read and write while optimistic revisions and idempotency protect semantic updates.
entries.evidence: The embedded concurrency gates run two processes against one SQLite store and require both writers to enter without losing events.

entries.text: Committing a bundle publishes the selected abouts to everyone who can read the repository. Export exact abouts deliberately; a full export from a shared user store can contain unrelated or private memory.
entries.evidence: Filtered export accepts repeatable exact abouts and refuses missing selections before writing the destination.

entries.text: ChronoLoom is local and capability-protected. The process binds to loopback, exchanges a random one-session URL capability for an HttpOnly cookie, and removes the token from the address. Moving the view never writes memory.
entries.evidence: The viewer and MCP App contracts separate read-only view state from memory writes and do not advertise a bare unauthorised URL.

entries.text: Use a plain file when the information is canonical prose, a large artifact or something people should edit directly. Use KMP when time, evidence, typed relations, supersession or cross-session recovery are part of the meaning.
entries.evidence: KMP is graph-temporal operational memory; it is not a replacement for source files or documentation.

entries.text: A decision can change without losing its history. In the worked Atlas example, offline work is required on September 1; SQLite is chosen for that reason on September 2. A central shared journal is required on September 5, and a later explicit decision replaces SQLite with PostgreSQL. The agent guide entry guide:kmp-agent:example:decision-history contains the sources and complete calls. Ask your agent to run this fictional example in an isolated store and open its about example:guide:decision-history in ChronoLoom. Select the new decision at Memories detail: one evidential link explains what it replaces, and one motivational link explains why it was chosen. Follow each to its original evidence. Compare September 3 with September 6 using an explicit clock; the new choice must not be projected into the past. Two memory kinds and two relation classes are justified by these sources. This lesson does not cover every kind or relationship, nor establish that a new writer LLM has learned to use KMP.
entries.evidence: The agent lesson includes four dated fictional sources, constraint and decision memories, explicit replacement and motivation links, temporal reads and a shared-view intent.

entries.text: An alias is not an account owner. In the second worked example, a signed source identifies Elena Vega as Nora, while an unqualified visitor-log mention of Nora remains unresolved. Separately, the account @oak is assigned to Jon and later to Rui. The assignment is replaced; Jon and Rui remain distinct people. Ask your agent to open the isolated example:guide:alias-ownership story in ChronoLoom after reading guide:kmp-agent:example:alias-ownership. Follow the same_entity_as link for the proven alias and the supersedes link for the account change; inspect their sources. Filtering the label Nora also includes the unidentified visitor, so a label is not identity proof. The example uses three observations and two assignment decisions because the sources justify them. It does not measure whether a new LLM will avoid an unsupported merge.
entries.evidence: The agent lesson preserves five literal fictional sources, the unresolved mention, separate identity and replacement links, and before/after assignment evidence.

entries.text: INC-17 contains an outage EVT-17-F and its later recovery EVT-17-R. Support reports the outage first; project later audits that same outage. Ask the agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:distributed-incident and run it in an isolated store. Open example:guide:incident-support in ChronoLoom and add example:guide:incident-project to the projection. Compare the initial observed view on September 1 with the late audit and reconciliation on September 2. Two observations, an error path and a success path have distinct roles. Shared labels find candidate pairs; the source-backed same_event_as link identifies only the two outage reports. Select its new support declaration, follow the edge and inspect its literal evidence. The recovery remains a separate event. Switch from observed to occurred to see why evidence learned on September 2 can describe an event on September 1; do not infer earlier knowledge from the event clock. The two abouts keep their original texts and ownership. This authored native example does not measure a new LLM writer.
entries.evidence: The lesson preserves four fictional sources, rejects unproved crossing and unsupported relation types, and compares per-about and shared timelines before and after an explicit equivalence.

entries.text: The TEMP-4 permit is signed on day one, first observed by a reviewer on day three and recorded by KMP on the real execution day four. It applies from day two until day five, exclusive. Ask the agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:four-clocks and resolve its calendar before running the isolated example:guide:four-clocks. Start in ChronoLoom at Atlas, narrow the occurred window, then choose Moment to inspect the permit and the signature check that supports it. Change the same window to observed: it is empty until you move to day three. Ingested shows the actual run day; validity on day two shows the applicable permit, not earlier knowledge of it. Follow the support edge and read the separate source and rationale. Moving the viewer does not change a native memory query or rewrite its clocks. The exercise uses a decision, an observation and feedback because the three sources have those roles; it does not measure a new writer LLM.
entries.evidence: The agent lesson resolves relative source dates from the actual UTC clock, keeps ingestion assigned by the kernel, and checks explicit read axes, interval boundaries and shared-view state.

entries.text: TRIP-7 has a transport charge, a corrected hotel invoice, a duplicate copy, a voided meal and a separate USD charge. Ask the agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:quantities and run the isolated lesson. In ChronoLoom start on September 1 observed time, before correction and cancellation. Then show the EUR source slice: six documents are not six expenses. Follow corrects from H-1 to H-0, same_event_as from H-1-C to H-1, and updates_state from the void to the meal. Finally select CALC-7: total_of points to 20.00 EUR and 35.00 EUR, while the incoming exclusion audit explains what was omitted and why. Follow that audit to its source documents. The subtotal is 55.00 EUR; 7.00 USD stays separate without a conversion rate. The agent calculates from inspected sources; KMP stores the value and proof, and writer acceptance does not check arithmetic. Moving the view does not rewrite earlier receipts or make the later total known sooner. This authored replay is not an LLM learning benchmark.
entries.evidence: The source-backed agent lesson records nine original memories and two new derived/audit memories, preserves original clocks, checks decimal operands and frames three stages with explicit observed intervals.

entries.text: SHIFT-6 has two reports assigning sole responsibility to Maya and Zoe for the same interval. Ask the agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:late-conflict and run the isolated lesson. In ChronoLoom start with R1, then show R2 and the unresolved review P1 on observed time before September 4. Select R2 to inspect contradicts and P1 to follow its two motivational links. The supported conclusion then is that the operator cannot be determined. A signed record L1 arrives September 5 for the September 1 shift; event time can show it beside the older reports, but it was not known sooner. The later review D1 confirms Maya, verified_by L1, and supersedes only R2 and P1. Follow both replacement targets and retain their original evidence. Compare historical observed recall before and after resolution; the panel labelled Current record includes later status and links, while the scene retains its selected clock and UTC window. Receipt order alone never chooses a winner. This authored example checks native behavior, not writer LLM learning.
entries.evidence: The source-backed lesson preserves five distinct memories, the before/after conflict proof and the original R2 clocks, with four temporal view stages.

entries.text: LEX-7 gives bitácora and journal one component meaning through an explicit glossary. Ask the agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:labels-negation and run the isolated lesson. Review S1 before and after relabelling: its Spanish text and original clocks stay intact, and English search returns the Spanish source. In the production RUN-7 view, S2 restates S1 while S3 says not enabled under the same instant and owner. Follow both relations; later receipt does not resolve their conflict. Inspect S4 in staging separately, then show all six component memories, including glossary constraint G1 and later RUN-8 decision D1. Opposite words from different environments or times do not create a universal contradiction. Labels group candidates; source-backed relations express what the writer knows. The Current record panel can show later links while the scene uses its selected observed window. This authored review does not measure LLM learning.
entries.evidence: The explicit glossary justifies replacing one component label, not rewriting the memory. Six native selector traversals preserve different conditions and an unresolved production disagreement.

entries.text: PACK-8 contains an export requirement, decision, test and result, plus unrelated warehouse lighting. Ask the agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:budget-proof. Review five typed memories in ChronoLoom and follow R1 verified_by T1, T1 uses_background D1 and D1 chosen_because C1. The temporal reader captures the inclusive start and continues two pages before excluding the exact end. A partial inspection preserves its object but may still omit proof: the agent must report the exact pending continuation and needed size. The viewer has its own reads and does not complete that MCP page. Packet membership creates no path to X1. Neither the sources nor two semantic UNKNOWN selections identify who authorized PURGE-9; stop rather than invent an approver. This authored native review does not measure independent LLM learning.
entries.evidence: The source-backed lesson retains five memories, typed path evidence, partial checkpoints and complete continuations with no semantic calls after the second UNKNOWN.

entries.text: HND-9 lets a fresh agent recover a saved constraint, decision and review request. Ask for guide:kmp-agent:example:shared-resumption. In ChronoLoom choose Observed and select C1. The agent reads your current revision, audits D1 to C1 and changes its focus without blindly restoring its old window. Repeating a completed intent returns the current view; a stale new intent conflicts. The view belongs to its serving process, while the source memories survive a fresh client. A click is not approval: separate source F1 confirms only the selection and leaves the offline test pending. Four source types and their evidence remain inspectable. The authored replay uses two native clients; independent LLM learning needs a separate evaluation.
entries.evidence: The lesson retains original clocks and sources, retries one logical decision without duplicating it, and distinguishes explicit feedback from human view gestures.

entries.text: Start with two source lines: a journal must accept writes offline, and SQLite is chosen for that reason. Ask your agent to read guide:kmp-agent:example:first-decision, record those two typed memories and show their chosen_because relation in ChronoLoom. The example proves a recorded choice, not a completed offline test. For a particular tool, memory kind or relation, use guide:kmp-agent:examples:by-capability. The other basic cases distinguish preference from requirement, approval from execution, and membership from evidence of a result.
entries.evidence: The first-decision lesson and the indexed basic cases contain explicit sources, native requests and limits; independent LLM learning remains a separate evaluation.

relations.evidence: The earlier observed view excludes the correction, duplicate and void; the final view adds the subtotal without altering that historical selection.

relations.why: The late duty record concerns an earlier shift, so the human review must distinguish event time from knowledge at receipt time.
relations.evidence: L1 occurred on September 1 and was observed on September 5; D1 is a September 5 decision and must not be moved back to the shift.

relations.why: After reviewing late conflict resolution, the reader distinguishes a contradiction that remains unresolved from unrelated opposite states selected by labels.
relations.evidence: No LEX-7 source resolves S1 versus S3; staging and the later maintenance decision remain separate contexts.

relations.why: The earlier label lesson distinguishes selection from proof; the budget lesson adds the difference between a page, a selection cap and missing evidence.
relations.evidence: A shared PACK-8 label groups export and warehouse records without supplying a semantic relation or authorization.

relations.why: A correct handoff preserves pending work and proof limits as well as the current shared frame.
relations.evidence: H1 and F1 leave the offline test pending; completing a view move never creates a test report.
